thread:
zhang: Quick brain-dump after pairing with Marcus — we observed some interesting edge cases when simulating partial network partitions between EU and US regions. Wanted to surface them here and propose a small refactor on handoff semantics.
marcus: Please do. Which cases stood out?
zhang: Two main ones: 1) dual-accept where both resident and fallback gateways accept a write because proxies diverged on cached policy, and 2) escape-loop where proxies keep toggling to escape mode and back under flapping connectivity leading to bursts of global writes.
anya: Those are bad. For dual-accept we must make gateway-level conflict resolution deterministic. Ideas: last-write-wins with vector clocks, or a lightweight primary lease per shard.
liam: Vector clocks are heavy; we already use causal tokens for some flows but not everywhere. A shard-level monotonic write-id from the resident gateway that's propagated during accept might be lighter. If a fallback accepts, it writes with a special escape-tag and an escrow record. Reconciler later inspects escrows and either completes or cancels.
marcus: So fallback writes would be provisionally accepted and put into an escrow table for reconciliation. That increases complexity but keeps availability.
sre-jen: Concern: escrow growth under sustained escaping. We need eviction/compaction rules and replay guarantees. Also operator visibility: percent-escrow-fulfillment within 1h.
zhang: For the escape-loop problem, we can add hysteresis: proxies require a sustained exceedance of latency/unreachability for T_down before enabling escape and a cool-down T_up before reverting. Also add a shared per-tenant escape-rate-budget to prevent constant toggling.
anya: Agreed. Also, can gateways annotate an accept with a "reconciliation_hint" that tells the reconciler which stream to inspect. That reduces scan windows.
marcus: For API boundary, let's keep control-plane authority over consent/escape_allowed, but allow dataplane to emit provisional escape-events that the control plane can reconcile and mutate. Control-plane should be the source of truth but not on the hot path.
liam: Small note on telemetry: add a metric for "dual_accept_conflicts" with tags (tenant, shard, region) so we can target high-conflict tenants.
ops-bot: chaos-bot: started partition simulation 2026-03-23T12:13Z. Monitoring conflict-metrics.
sre-jen: Operational checklist item: add a runbook for when reconciler backlog > 5k escrows: steps to throttle new escapes, scale reconciler, and optionally put tenant in manual quarantine.
zhang: I'll draft the reconciler design and the escrow lifecycle (write->provisional->reconcile->either merge or tombstone). Will include TTLs and compaction heuristics.
marcus: Thanks. Please include storage cost estimate per 1M escrows. Also include required idempotency constraints for gateways.
anya: I'll help with telemetry mappings and threshold proposals.
marcus: Ok let's land this as a follow-up RFC and implement small reconciler in staging. Action items: zhang: reconciler design, anya: telemetry, liam: gateway idempotency checks, sre-jen: runbook skeleton. Will sync next week.
